subject: EdgeFlow reference blueprint & validation milestones
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya@edgeflow.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: dan.kim@edgeflow.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: EdgeFlow + Redwood — request: reference architecture + validation scope

Hi Jonas / Lauren,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — excited about the potential to standardize the connector between EdgeFlow's ingestion pipeline and Redwood's hosted/dedicated runtimes. We discussed a few architecture alternatives (direct VPC peering, shared private endpoints, and tokenized API proxy). To move forward with procurement and engineering alignment on our side we need: a concise reference architecture you recommend for a hybrid deployment (hosted API with VPC-peered private endpoints for PII workloads), and a validation/test plan we can run in our sandbox over a two-week window.

Specifically from Redwood we need: 
- A reference blueprint (network layout, auth flow, expected latencies, and fallback behavior)
- A test matrix with pass/fail criteria (throughput, cold-start latency, KV cache behavior, and failure injection)
- A quick checklist for required infra changes on EdgeFlow's side (Firewall rules, VPC route tables, certs, etc.)

We can share our sandbox credentials and a sample dataset once we have the test plan. Attaching our compliance checklist for reference (see later in thread).

Thanks,
Priya Rao
Solutions Architect | EdgeFlow Systems
priya@edgeflow.ai
+1 415-555-0132

Attachments: edgeflow-compliance-checklist.pdf
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Priya Rao <priya@edgeflow.ai>, Daniel Kim <dan.kim@edgeflow.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EdgeFlow + Redwood — request: reference architecture + validation scope

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. Lauren and I put together an initial reference blueprint and a scoped test matrix that should cover the items you called out. Attaching: redwood_edgeflow_reference_blueprint_v1.pdf and edgeflow-test-matrix.xlsx.

High-level summary here so your engineering team can scan quickly:
- Recommended deployment: Hosted Redwood API for non-PII traffic; Dedicated Reserved nodes in your VPC via private endpoints for PII/regulated calls.
- Auth: mTLS between EdgeFlow proxy and Redwood private endpoint + token exchange for user-level audit traces.
- SLO goals for validation: 95th percentile latency < 120ms on cached requests; cold-start 99th < 400ms on dedicated nodes; throughput target 350 req/s per pool for the sample dataset.
- Fallback behavior: requests routed to a compatible quantized model (cost tier) when dedicated pool saturated; audit logging retained for 90 days (configurable).

Proposed validation milestones (two-week window):
1) Week 0: infra prep (VPC peering/VPN + certs) — EdgeFlow owner: Daniel
2) Week 1: functionality & latency smoke (small dataset) — Redwood owner: Lauren
3) Week 2: scale and failure injection (chaos tests + burst) — Redwood owner: Jonas / Sergio

Can we lock a Monday start (Nov 16) for the two-week run? If that is tight we can also start Nov 18.

I'll loop Sergio and Marissa into the technical runbook next (they'll own load/failure tests and runbook docs).

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_edgeflow_reference_blueprint_v1.pdf, edgeflow-test-matrix.xlsx
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: EdgeFlow validation — owners, runbook, and quick asks

Team — moving the EdgeFlow engagement into runbook mode. Quick context: EdgeFlow wants a hybrid reference (hosted + dedicated VPC endpoints) and a two-week validation window starting the week of Nov 16 (target). See attachments I sent them (blueprint + test matrix).

Action items:
- Sergio: lead scale & failure injection scenarios. Responsible for creating the harness (k6 + local chaos) and the infra scripts to ramp GPUs. Deliverable: INFR-3312 test job linked in Jira.
- Marissa: validate compatibility for our RDKit-style tokenization and ensure the quantized fallback models are acceptable for their accuracy targets. Deliverable: short summary doc + baseline eval by Nov 13.
- Lauren: own infra prep (VPC peering checklist, cert exchange, and private endpoint config). Coordinate with Daniel at EdgeFlow for their firewall rules.

Constraints / Notes:
- We must avoid changing any model weights for the test; only configuration and batching/quantization adjustments.
- Audit log retention for the run should be set to 90 days; security will request the logs post-run.
- If we see sustained queueing (> 30s) we will trigger the canary fallback and record token-level costs.

I've created the HubSpot deal and Jira ticket for tracking: HUB-4921 / INFR-3312 (links attached below). Let's hit the deliverables by EOD Nov 13 for the prep phase.

Jonas
From: Priya Rao <priya@edgeflow.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: dan.kim@edgeflow.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EdgeFlow reference blueprint & validation milestones

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our infra team after a quick review: 
- We can do VPC peering but prefer to use private endpoints behind our internal proxy (EdgeFlow API gateway). Can you confirm Redwood supports private endpoint DNS inside our VPC (no NAT)?
- For auth, EdgeFlow prefers a short-lived token exchange (OIDC) in addition to mTLS for service-to-service ops. Are you able to support OIDC token introspection in the private flow?
- Sandbox availability: we can open a dedicated test VPC Nov 15–30 and provide temporary IAM creds.

We're happy to start the validation window Nov 16. Daniel will be our technical point for the infra prep. He is on this thread.

On scheduling: can we do a 30-minute runbook sync this Thursday (Nov 12) at 9am PT to align owners and confirm the checklist?

Best,
Priya
